summary: Teton County site on the Teton National Forest that was to be manned in July 1954; no readable source documents its structure or what remains.

facts.status_note: Listed among unknown/undocumented sites with no coordinates; no readable source confirms a lookout structure.

events.note: Jackson Hole Courier item (July 15, 1954, quoted on westlookouts.weebly.com) said the Two-Ocean Plateau position would be manned within the following week. This is a planned staffing notice, not a record of how long it was used.

corrections.why: The Teton National Forest was consolidated with the Bridger National Forest on July 1, 1973 into one forest that is now called Bridger-Teton. The brief uses the 1954 name, which no longer describes the current managing forest. The story now uses the 1954 name only as 'what was then the Teton National Forest'.

notes_for_editor: The only dated material is the July 15, 1954 Jackson Hole Courier notice, quoted secondhand on westlookouts.weebly.com; the original was not found. It names the plateau as a position to be manned within the week, not as a confirmed lookout with a structure. No construction, design or closing date is in any readable source, so none is recorded. The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it under its Unknown/Undocumented Sites heading, with no coordinates. The Teton history report does not mention a Two-Ocean Plateau lookout, so it is not cited for that. The Teton NF name in the brief is the 1954 name; a correction to Bridger-Teton is proposed and the story now reflects it. Story is about 195 words.
